payload.title: Blocking the electron transport chain

stimulus.description: Cyanide is a poison that binds to the last protein of the electron transport chain in mitochondria and prevents it from passing electrons to oxygen. A cell that is exposed to cyanide is supplied with glucose and oxygen.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Describe the role of the electron transport chain in aerobic cellular respiration.
parts.model_answer: The chain passes electrons through a series of proteins to oxygen and uses the energy released to pump protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane.

required_elements: The electron transport chain passes electrons along proteins and pumps protons across the inner membrane to build a gradient
alt_solutions: electrons move to oxygen as energy is used to pump protons
the chain builds a proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane
common_errors: says the chain makes glucose
says the chain occurs in the cytoplasm
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Explain how the movement of protons through ATP synthase results in the production of ATP.
parts.model_answer: Protons move down their gradient through ATP synthase, and the energy released drives the addition of a phosphate to ADP.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives a correct explanation of how or why the process works

alt_solutions: the proton gradient provides the energy for ATP synthase to produce ATP
chemiosmosis couples proton flow to ATP formation

says ATP is produced by moving electrons to ATP synthase

parts.prompt: Predict the effect of cyanide on the rate of ATP production by the mitochondria.

common_errors: predicts that ATP production increases

parts.label: D

payload.title: Analyzing a model of DNA replication

stimulus.description: The diagram shows the two parental template strands at a replication fork that is moving toward the left side of the diagram.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Identify which template strand (top or bottom) is used to make the leading strand.
parts.model_answer: The top template strand is used to make the leading strand.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the template strand for the leading strand
required_elements: States that the top template strand is the template for the continuously made leading strand
alt_solutions: the top strand's new strand is made continuously toward the fork
leading strand template: top
common_errors: names the bottom strand
names both strands
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Explain why the new strand made on the other template strand is made in short fragments.
parts.model_answer: DNA polymerase adds nucleotides only to the 3' end of a growing strand, so on the template whose new strand is made away from the fork, synthesis must be restarted in short Okazaki fragments as the fork opens.

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains that synthesis only occurs in the 5' to 3' direction away from the fork on the lagging template
required_elements: DNA polymerase adds nucleotides only to the 3' end, so that new strand runs away from the fork and is made in fragments
alt_solutions: synthesis is always 5' to 3' and the lagging strand must be made in pieces as the fork opens
the strand grows away from the fork, so it is made in Okazaki fragments
common_errors: says DNA polymerase works in both directions
says the lagging strand is made in fragments because it has no primer
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Write the base sequence of the new strand that pairs with the top template strand, from the left end of the diagram to the right end, and label its left and right ends as 5' or 3'.
parts.model_answer: Left to right the new strand is CTGCGATT, with its left end 3' and its right end 5'.

rubric_rows.criterion: Writes the complementary sequence with the correct 5' and 3' labels
required_elements: Writes CTGCGATT from left to right and labels the left end 3' and the right end 5'
alt_solutions: CTGCGATT with ends 3' and 5'
complementary bases written in the same left-to-right positions with antiparallel labels
common_errors: writes the correct bases but labels the ends the same as the template
uses uracil or the wrong complementary bases
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Explain how the antiparallel structure of DNA and the direction of DNA polymerase activity relate to the way a DNA molecule is copied.
parts.model_answer: Because the two strands run in opposite directions and polymerase works only 5' to 3', one strand is copied continuously and the other in fragments, but each new molecule still has one old and one new strand.

rubric_rows.criterion: Links antiparallel strands and 5' to 3' synthesis to leading and lagging strand synthesis
required_elements: Opposite orientations of the strands and 5' to 3' synthesis explain why one strand is continuous and the other is made in fragments
alt_solutions: antiparallel strands plus one-directional polymerase give a leading and a lagging strand
the structure of DNA requires different mechanisms for copying each strand
common_errors: says both strands are copied in the same way
says replication produces two completely new molecules
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

review.summary: The bundle fits the topic and its numbers are correct. Part C's key and rubric are incomplete: they accept a pH 4 versus pH 7 comparison alone and do not require comparison with pH 10 or a caveat about the three tested levels. Part A's rubric is also loose. Fail on key and scoring, flagged as missing_condition.

scope_skill.notes: The bundle as a whole fits 3.2 and 4.B. Part A is a 4.B description. B, C and D use other skills, which is acceptable for a bundle.

key_scoring.notes: Part C asks whether the claim "greatest activity at pH 7" is supported. The model answer and rubric compare only pH 4 and pH 7. They never require comparing pH 7 with pH 10, although a "greatest" claim requires comparison with all tested levels. The rubric lets a response that checks only pH 4 earn the point, which is an incomplete test of the claim. The claim is also stated as a causal claim about the enzyme's greatest activity, but only three pH values were tested, so the true optimum is not established. The rubric ignores this limit, and the solver raised it. Part B's tolerance of ±2.1 is fine. Part A's rubric is vague: it does not require pH 7 to be named as the greatest, and requires_numbers is false even though the prompt asks for values.
